title: MYP Individuals and Societies Revision Plan
summary: MYP Individuals and Societies revision made practical: learn what to practise, use assessment criteria to improve, and manage eAssessment time.
body_markdown:
Preparing for an on-screen examination can feel strangely intangible. There is no single stack of facts that guarantees success. You need knowledge, but you must also investigate, communicate and think critically while a clock quietly keeps moving.


Effective **MYP Individuals and Societies revision** therefore has two parts. First, strengthen your understanding of the topics taught in your course. Second, practise turning that understanding into criterion-focused answers under timed conditions. The aim is not to memorise everything. It is to make good academic decisions reliably.


The IB states that MYP on-screen examinations last between 1 hour 45 minutes and 2 hours, depending on the subject. Its published Individuals and Societies subject brief describes a 2-hour examination built around three tasks. Because specifications can change, confirm the current arrangements with your school before planning exact timings.


### Your MYP Individuals and Societies revision checklist


A balanced preparation plan should include:


- revising key concepts, examples and subject vocabulary
- interpreting written, visual, statistical and map-based sources
- forming focused research questions and investigation plans
- evaluating sources for origin, purpose, value and limitations
- constructing arguments supported by specific evidence
- comparing perspectives rather than merely describing them
- practising command terms and on-screen response skills
- using the assessment criteria to review every substantial answer
- completing timed sections and full mock examinations


The[MYP Individuals and Societies assessment guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-individuals-and-societies-assessment) provides a useful starting point if you are unsure how these skills fit together.


### Understand what the eAssessment is testing


Individuals and Societies may draw on disciplines such as history, geography and economics. Yet the examination is not simply a memory test for one discipline. Questions can provide unfamiliar source material and ask you to apply concepts or methods developed during your course.


The official IB subject brief describes three broad tasks. The investigating task involves evaluating an investigation and planning one. Other tasks assess communication and critical thinking alongside knowledge and understanding. This means revision should resemble the work you will perform, not just the notes you want to remember.


Begin by reviewing[how MYP Individuals and Societies is assessed](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-individuals-and-societies-is-assessed) . Then organise your revision around four recurring criteria:


Criterion What your practice should develop


A: Knowing and understanding Accurate terminology, relevant examples and clear explanations


B: Investigating Focused questions, justified methods and effective research planning


C: Communicating Logical structure, appropriate formats and clear documentation of sources


D: Thinking critically Analysis, evaluation, synthesis and recognition of perspectives


All four matter. A knowledgeable answer can still underperform if it lacks structure or analysis. Equally, polished evaluation cannot replace missing subject knowledge.


### What to practise each week


### Build usable knowledge


Create a topic map for each unit. Include important concepts, processes, events, places, people and examples, but connect them rather than listing them. For urbanisation, for example, you might connect migration, employment, housing pressure, infrastructure and environmental change.


Use RevisionDojo **Study Notes** to clarify difficult material, then test recall with **Flashcards** . Retrieval should be followed by application. After recalling a concept, explain how it could illuminate a source, case study or unfamiliar scenario.


RevisionDojo’s subject resources can help you move between disciplinary perspectives. Its guides to[MYP History criteria](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-history-number-of-criteria) and the broader[Individuals and Societies criteria](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-individuals-and-societies-number-of-criteria) are particularly useful when checking what strong subject-specific reasoning looks like.


### Analyse varied sources


Choose one source at a time: a map, chart, photograph, speech, article extract or table. Give yourself 5 minutes to annotate it. Identify its message, supporting details, context and possible limitations.


Then write one analytical paragraph. A simple internal structure works well:


1. Make a claim that answers the question.
2. Select precise evidence from the source.
3. Explain what the evidence suggests.
4. Connect it to relevant contextual knowledge.
5. Add a qualification or alternative interpretation when appropriate.


Do not treat every source as either reliable or unreliable. A source can be valuable for one purpose and limited for another. Evaluation becomes stronger when you specify what the source helps a researcher understand.


A student evaluates an old map while a detective questions a giant wall clock


### Plan investigations


Criterion B deserves dedicated practice. Take a broad topic and turn it into a focused research question. Then identify the information required, suitable methods, possible sources and a practical sequence of steps.


Compare these questions:


- How does tourism affect cities?
- To what extent did tourism change employment patterns in a selected city between two specified years?


The second is more manageable because it defines an issue, location, measure and period. A strong investigation plan should also explain *why* each method is suitable. Naming interviews, surveys or secondary data is not enough without justification.


### Practise arguments, not answer shapes


Command terms tell you what intellectual action to perform. “Describe” requires relevant characteristics. “Explain” requires reasons or mechanisms. “Compare and contrast” requires similarities and differences. “Evaluate” requires a supported judgement about strengths and limitations.


Build a command-term bank and attach a short checklist to each term. RevisionDojo’s[guide to MYP Criteria A-D](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-criteria-a-b-c-d-explained) can help translate broad descriptors into actions you can see in your writing.


The **Questionbank** is useful here because you can practise one skill repeatedly rather than waiting to complete another full examination. When an answer feels uncertain, **AI Chat** can help you question the logic, while **Grading tools** can expose where your response stops describing and starts, or fails to start, analysing.


### Use the criteria to self-assess


Self-assessment works best when it is diagnostic. Giving yourself a level and moving on changes little. Instead, collect evidence from your answer.


After each response, highlight:


- accurate knowledge and terminology for Criterion A
- research decisions and their justification for Criterion B
- organisation, format and source acknowledgement for Criterion C
- analysis, evidence, perspectives and judgement for Criterion D


Next, read the relevant descriptor supplied by your teacher. Ask which words in the descriptor your answer visibly demonstrates. If a descriptor expects detailed analysis, underline the details and analytical links. If you cannot find them, the answer is not there yet.


Write one specific improvement instruction, such as: “After every source quotation, explain how it supports the claim.” Avoid vague comments such as “add detail.” The[guide to balancing Individuals and Societies with other MYP subjects](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/balancing-myp-individuals-and-societies-other-subjects) can also help you schedule these review cycles without letting one subject consume the week.


### Manage time without rushing every answer


Time management begins before the mock examination. First, complete individual questions without a limit so you can learn the method. Then introduce generous limits. Finally, practise under realistic conditions using **Predicted Papers** and **Mock Exams** .


For a confirmed 2-hour examination, a sensible starting framework is:


- reserve 5-10 minutes to inspect the tasks and sources
- allocate time according to the demands and available marks
- leave several minutes for checking incomplete responses, evidence and clarity


Do not divide time equally by question count. A short identification question should not receive the same attention as an extended evaluation. Use marks, command terms and answer complexity to decide when to move on.


During practice, record planned time and actual time for each task. If one response repeatedly expands beyond its value, set a stopping rule. For example, finish the current analytical point, add a concise judgement and continue. An unfinished perfect answer is usually a costly bargain.


### A four-week preparation plan


### Week 1: Diagnose and organise


Review the assessment criteria, complete a short mixed task and identify your weakest criterion. Build topic maps and begin daily retrieval with Study Notes and Flashcards.


### Week 2: Train individual skills


Alternate source analysis, investigation planning and evidence-based paragraphs. Use the Questionbank and check every answer against one criterion. The[RevisionDojo Individuals and Societies resource guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-for-myp-individuals-and-societies) can help you choose tools for each weakness.


### Week 3: Combine skills under time limits


Complete longer task sets. Practise moving from source interpretation to contextual knowledge and judgement. Review mistakes through the criteria instead of merely counting marks.


### Week 4: Simulate and refine


Complete full Mock Exams in the on-screen format available to you. Review each attempt with Grading tools, your teacher’s guidance and the official descriptors. Revisit only the knowledge and skills that the evidence shows need attention.


### Preparation becomes calmer when it becomes specific


The hardest part of MYP revision is often uncertainty. Students know they should “revise,” but the word conceals too many different jobs.


A criterion-led plan makes those jobs visible. Learn the content. Analyse sources. Design investigations. Communicate clearly. Evaluate perspectives. Then practise doing all five while managing the clock.


RevisionDojo brings that process together through its Questionbank, Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, Grading tools, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, Coursework Library and Tutors. The tools matter because each one answers a different preparation problem. Used deliberately, they turn revision from repeated reading into evidence of progress.
